DECISION AND OPINION ON REVIEW 
Timely Petition for Review under §19(b) having been filed by the Respondent herein 
and notice given to all parties, the Commission, after considering the issues of causal connection, 
medical expenses, prospective medical care, and any other issues presented within the arbitration 
transcript, and being advised of the facts and law, affirms and adopts the Decision of the 
Arbitrator, which is attached hereto and made a part hereof.  The Commission further remands 
this case to the Arbitrator for further proceedings for a determination of a further amount of 
temporary total compensation or of compensation for permanent disability, if any, pursuant to 
Thomas v. Industrial Commission, 78 Ill.2d 327, 399 N.E.2d 1322, 35 Ill.Dec. 794 (1980). 
IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED BY THE COMMISSION that the Decision of the 
Arbitrator filed September 5, 2025, is hereby affirmed and adopted. 
IT IS FURTHER ORDERED BY THE COMMISSION that this case be remanded to the 
Arbitrator for further proceedings consistent with this Decision, but only after the latter of 
expiration of the time for filing a written request for Summons to the Circuit Court has expired 
without the filing of such a written request, or after the time of completion of any judicial 
proceedings, if such a written request has been filed.

IT IS FURTHER ORDERED BY THE COMMISSION that Respondent pay to Petitioner 
interest under §19(n) of the Act, if any. 
 
 
IT IS FURTHER ORDERED BY THE COMMISSION that Respondent shall have credit 
for all amounts paid, if any, to or on behalf of Petitioner on account of said accidental injury. 
 
Bond for removal of this cause to the Circuit Court by Respondent is hereby fixed at the 
sum of $100.00.  The party commencing the proceedings for review in the Circuit Court shall file 
with the Commission a Notice of Intent to File for Review in Circuit Court.

An Application for Adjustment of Claim was filed in this matter, and a Notice of Hearing was mailed to each 
party.  The matter was heard by the Honorable William R. Gallagher, Arbitrator of the Commission, in the city 
of Mt. Vernon, on July 25, 2025.  After reviewing all of the evidence presented, the Arbitrator hereby makes 
findings on the disputed issues checked below, and attaches those findings to this document. 
 
DISPUTED ISSUES 
 
A. 
 Was Respondent operating under and subject to the Illinois Workers' Compensation or Occupational  
 
 Diseases Act? 
 
B. 
 Was there an employee-employer relationship? 
 
C. 
 Did an accident occur that arose out of and in the course of Petitioner's employment by Respondent? 
 
D. 
 What was the date of the accident?

FINDINGS 
 
On the date of accident, April 20, 2023, Respondent was operating under and subject to the provisions of the Act.   
 
On this date, an employee-employer relationship did exist between Petitioner and Respondent.   
 
On this date, Petitioner did sustain an accident that arose out of and in the course of employment. 
 
Timely notice of this accident was given to Respondent. 
 
Petitioner's current condition of ill-being is causally related to the accident.  
 
In the year preceding the injury, Petitioner earned $67,279.24; the average weekly wage was $1,293.83.  
 
On the date of accident, Petitioner was 61 years of age, single with 0 dependent child(ren). 
 
Respondent has paid all reasonable and necessary charges for all reasonable and necessary medical services.  
 
Respondent shall be given a credit of $100,671.89 for TTD, $0.00 for TPD, $0.00 for maintenance, and $0.00 for 
other benefits, for a total credit of $100,671.89.   
 
Respondent is entitled to a credit of $0.00 under Section 8(j) of the Act. 
 
ORDER 
 
Respondent shall authorize and pay for prospective medical treatment, including but not limited to, diagnostic 
tests and right shoulder arthroscopic surgery, as recommended by Dr. Robert Bell. 
 
 
In no instance shall this award be a bar to subsequent hearing and determination of an additional amount of 
medical benefits or compensation for a temporary or permanent disability, if any.   
 
RULES REGARDING APPEALS      Unless a party files a Petition for Review within 30 days after receipt of this 
decision, and perfects a review in accordance with the Act and Rules, then this decision shall be entered as the 
decision of the Commission.   
 
STATEMENT OF INTEREST RATE      If the Commission reviews this award, interest at the rate set forth on the 
Notice of Decision of Arbitrator shall accrue from the date listed below to the day before the date of payment; 
however, if an employee's appeal results in either no change or a decrease in this award, interest shall not accrue.

Dan Koetting v. TMS International                                                   23 WC 26445 
Page 3 
Findings of Fact 
 
Petitioner filed an Application for Adjustment of Claim which alleged he sustained an accidental 
injury arising out of and in the course of his employment by Respondent on April 20, 2023. 
According to the Application, Petitioner "Climbed steps, slipped and fell, caught right shoulder" 
and sustained in injury to his "Right shoulder; Man as a Whole" (Arbitrator's Exhibit 2). This case 
was tried in a 19(b) proceeding and Petitioner sought an order for prospective medical treatment. 
The prospective medical treatment sought by Petitioner was diagnostic tests and right shoulder 
arthroscopic surgery, as recommended by Dr. Robert Bell, an orthopedic surgeon. Respondent 
disputed liability on the basis of causal relationship as well as the reasonableness and medical 
necessity of the prospective medical treatment being sought by Petitioner (Arbitrator's Exhibit 1). 
 
Petitioner's entitlement to temporary total disability benefits was not a disputed issue at trial; 
however, Petitioner claimed he was entitled to temporary total disability benefits of 117 6/7 weeks, 
commencing April 22, 2023, through July 25, 2025 (date of trial). Respondent stipulated Petitioner 
was entitled to the temporary total disability benefits claimed by him (Arbitrator's Exhibit 1). 
 
Petitioner worked for Respondent as a crane operator. On April 20, 2023, Petitioner was in the 
process of climbing down a ladder adjacent to the crane. Petitioner testified the steps on the ladder 
were covered with oil. At the time Petitioner was climbing down the ladder, both of his arms were 
extended overhead. Because of the oil on the steps, Petitioner slipped and he attempted to grab the 
rung above him with his right hand. When he did so, Petitioner hyperextended his right 
arm/shoulder. 
 
Petitioner initially sought medical treatment the following day, April 21, 2023, at Gateway 
Occupational Medicine, where he was evaluated by Mitra Shultz, a Physician Assistant. PA Shultz 
diagnosed Petitioner with right shoulder pain, imposed work/activity restrictions and referred 
Petitioner to Dr. Lyndon Gross, an orthopedic surgeon (Petitioner's Exhibit 1). There was no 
evidence Petitioner was ever evaluated by Dr. Gross. 
 
Petitioner was evaluated by Dr. Robert Bell, an orthopedic surgeon, on May 8, 2023. At that time, 
Petitioner informed Dr. Bell of the work-related accident and complained of right shoulder pain. 
Petitioner also advised Dr. Bell that he had previously undergone rotator cuff surgery on the left 
shoulder five years prior, but had no prior right shoulder problems. On examination, Dr. Bell noted 
Petitioner had positive impingement of the right shoulder as well as some weakness of the 
supraspinatus and infraspinatus on the right. He diagnosed Petitioner with biceps tendinitis and 
rotator cuff impingement syndrome. Dr. Bell prescribed medication and ordered physical therapy 
(Petitioner's Exhibit 2). 
 
When Dr. Bell saw Petitioner on June 5, 2023, Petitioner advised the physical therapy had helped 
some, but he continued to have right shoulder pain. Dr. Bell noted Petitioner could not undergo an 
MRI scan, so he ordered an ultrasound of Petitioner's right shoulder (Petitioner's Exhibit 2). 
 
The ultrasound was performed on Petitioner's right shoulder on June 26, 2023. According to the 
radiologist, the ultrasound revealed tendinosis of the subscapularis, tiny intrasubstance tears of the 
26IWCC0140

Dan Koetting v. TMS International                                                   23 WC 26445 
Page 4 
supraspinatus, but no evidence of a full thickness tear, and a possible partial thickness tear of the 
infraspinatus (Petitioner's Exhibit 3). 
 
Dr. Bell saw Petitioner on July 10, 2023, and he reviewed the ultrasound. Dr. Bell's interpretation 
of the ultrasound was consistent with that of the radiologist. He diagnosed Petitioner with a partial 
thickness rotator cuff tear and opined Petitioner had a 60/80% chance of resolution with rest and 
therapy. However, he also noted that if Petitioner did not improve over time, an arthroscopic 
decompression and graft might be indicated (Petitioner's Exhibit 2). 
 
Petitioner initially received physical therapy from May 17, 2023, through August 16, 2023. In the 
physical therapy note of July 26, 2023, Petitioner advised the therapist that he had recently had 
two 13/14 hour drives and he was only able to minimally use his right hand because of right 
anterior shoulder pain. In the physical therapy record of August 14, 2023, it was noted Petitioner 
had been at Kentucky Lake, and, because of the driving time, his right shoulder was stiff 
(Petitioner's Exhibit 7; pp 56, 61). 
 
At trial, Petitioner was questioned about his driving for 13/14 hours, and he advised that he drove 
south to transport the ashes of his wife who had died the preceding year. In respect to his trip to 
Kentucky Lake, Petitioner responded that it was about a four hour drive each way and he 
customarily took a weeklong vacation there every year. 
 
Dr. Bell saw Petitioner on August 24, 2023. At that time, Dr. Bell reaffirmed his diagnosis of 
Petitioner's right shoulder condition, and noted that, in spite of months of therapy and rest, 
Petitioner continued to experience right shoulder pain. Dr. Bell recommended Petitioner proceed 
with arthroscopic surgery of the right shoulder and indicated that if he found a small full thickness 
tear, he would do a debridement repair and a biceps tenodesis. If he found evidence of just a partial 
thickness tear and a positive bubble test to the intrasubstance tear, he would then perform a graft 
over that area (Petitioner's Exhibit 2). 
 
Dr. Bell saw Petitioner on November 30, 2023, and Petitioner's right shoulder condition remained 
essentially the same. Dr. Bell again noted that conservative treatment had failed and he renewed 
his recommendation Petitioner undergo arthroscopic surgery (Petitioner's Exhibit 2). 
 
At the direction of Respondent, Petitioner was examined by Dr. Nathan Mall, an orthopedic 
surgeon, on October 18, 2023. In connection with his examination of Petitioner, Dr. Mall reviewed 
medical records provided to him by Respondent. When seen by Dr. Mall, Petitioner informed him 
about the accident of April 20, 2023, and complained of right shoulder pain. Dr. Mall's examination 
of Petitioner revealed a decreased range of motion and pain over the biceps tendon and AC joint. 
He diagnosed Petitioner with a right shoulder traction injury and likely superior labral tear with 
biceps tendinopathy. In respect to treatment, Dr. Mall questioned why steroid injections had not 
been performed, but opined an AC joint resection and biceps tenodesis were appropriate, as well 
as a possible augmentation patch. He also opined that further surgical procedures might be 
indicated, depending upon the extent of the tears (Respondent's Exhibit 3; Deposition Exhibit 2). 
 
Dr. Bell performed arthroscopic surgery on Petitioner's right shoulder on January 12, 2024. The 
procedure consisted of debridement and repair of a full thickness tear of the upper 1/3 of the 
26IWCC0140

Dan Koetting v. TMS International                                                   23 WC 26445 
Page 5 
subscapularis, and debridement and repair of a near full thickness tear of the supraspinatus with a 
graft. The post operative diagnosis was rotator cuff tear and SLAP tear of the right shoulder 
(Petitioner's Exhibit 6). 
 
Dr. Bell saw Petitioner on February 15, 2024. At that time, Dr. Bell noted healing of the right 
shoulder and a smooth arc of motion. He directed Petitioner to discontinue immobilization of the 
shoulder and ordered physical therapy (Petitioner's Exhibit 2). 
 
Petitioner received physical therapy from February 22, 2024, through June 6, 2024. In the physical 
therapy record of March 11, 2024, it was noted Petitioner's range of motion was getting better, but 
Petitioner complained of constant pain (Petitioner's Exhibit 7; p 101). 
 
Dr. Bell evaluated Petitioner on March 28, 2024, and May 9, 2024. When he saw Petitioner on 
May 9, 2024, he noted Petitioner was progressing slowly and Petitioner complained of 
weakness/stiffness in certain positions. He directed Petitioner to continue physical therapy 
(Petitioner's Exhibit 2). 
 
Petitioner continued physical therapy (work hardening/conditioning) from June 26, 2024, through 
July 29, 2024. In the physical therapy record of July 10, 2024, it was noted Petitioner complained 
of low back pain and that Petitioner continued to experience right arm pain/stiffness. When seen 
on July 29, 2024, Petitioner advised he was able to use his right arm for light activity, but felt he 
was limited in regard to what heavy lifting and work he could do. The record of that date noted 
Petitioner's low back symptoms had interfered with his ability to fully participate in work 
conditioning on several occasions (Petitioner's Exhibit 7; pp 196, 215). At trial, Petitioner testified 
he terminated work conditioning at that time because of his low back and left leg pain. 
 
Dr. Bell saw Petitioner on August 1, 2024. At that time, Dr. Bell noted Petitioner had begun work 
hardening, but was having difficulties because of back issues. Dr. Bell ordered another ultrasound 
of Petitioner's right shoulder (Petitioner's Exhibit 2). 
 
At the direction of Respondent, Petitioner was again examined by Dr. Mall on August 14, 2024. 
In connection with his examination of Petitioner, Dr. Mall reviewed up-to-date medical records as 
well as prior medical records regarding Petitioner's prior left shoulder surgery. In his review of the 
prior medical records, Dr. Mall noted Petitioner was diagnosed with type II diabetes and had been 
noncompliant with his diabetic diet and inconsistently reporting whether he was or was not 
smoking cigarettes (Respondent's Exhibit 3; Deposition Exhibit 3). 
 
In respect to Petitioner's right shoulder issues, Dr. Mall recommended Petitioner undergo a repeat 
ultrasound to evaluate the integrity of the repair. If the tendon was determined to be healed, Dr. 
Mall recommended Petitioner undergo a steroid injection followed by physical therapy. If the 
rotator cuff was determined not to be healed, Dr. Mall opined a revision procedure might be 
necessary. Dr. Mall also opined diabetes and smoking are risk factors for healing from surgery, 
especially rotator cuff surgery. He also noted Petitioner complained of pain with any type of 
maneuver of the shoulder, had good strength, but would give up on resistance, complaining of 
significant pain (Respondent's Exhibit 3; Deposition Exhibit 3). 
 
26IWCC0140

Dan Koetting v. TMS International                                                   23 WC 26445 
Page 6 
The ultrasound of Petitioner's right shoulder was performed on September 18, 2024. According to 
the radiologist, the study revealed insertional subscapularis tendinopathy with likely suture anchor, 
a small area of partial thickness articular sided tearing, supraspinatus and infraspinatus cuff 
tendinopathy, a proximal 6 X 4 mm partial thickness articular sided tear of the anterior 
supraspinatus, ossification involving the posterior infraspinatus and moderate subacromial 
subdeltoid bursitis (Petitioner's Exhibit 4). 
 
Dr. Bell saw Petitioner on October 17, 2024. At that time, he reviewed the ultrasound of September 
18, 2024. Dr. Bell's interpretation of its findings was consistent with that of the radiologist. Dr. 
Bell directed Petitioner to resume physical therapy/work hardening (Petitioner's Exhibit 2). 
 
Petitioner received physical therapy/work hardening from November 5, 2024, through December 
2, 2024. During this time, Petitioner continued to complain of pain/stiffness in the right shoulder 
and advised he limited his use of the right shoulder/arm because of the pain (Petitioner's Exhibit 
7; pp 226-257). 
 
Dr. Bell evaluated Petitioner on November 21, 2024. On examination, Dr. Bell noted Petitioner 
had pain with resisted subscapularis, but no weakness, "giving way" when he stressed the 
infraspinatus and supraspinatus, and pain with resisted supraspinatus. He again reviewed the 
findings of the ultrasound of September 18, 2024. At that time, Dr. Bell made the recommendation 
Petitioner undergo another arthroscopic surgery of the right shoulder, put an anchor in to suture 
down the corner of the supraspinatus and possibly repeat graft over the area, as well as a possible 
repeat bursectomy (Petitioner's Exhibit 2). 
 
At the direction of Respondent, Dr. Mall reviewed up-to-date medical records which included the 
report of the ultrasound performed on September 18, 2024, and he prepared an addendum report 
dated March 20, 2025. In respect of his review of the ultrasound, he noted it revealed a 6 X 4 mm 
partial thickness articular sided tear of the anterior supraspinatus which he described as being 
"extremely small." He also noted Dr. Bell had recommended repeat arthroscopy of the right 
shoulder (Respondent's Exhibit 3; Deposition Exhibit 4). 
 
Dr. Mall opined the partial thickness tear he observed in the ultrasound was "…essentially a normal 
finding" and not something which would cause give-way weakness and severe pain. Dr. Mall 
opined the findings of the ultrasound did not support another surgical intervention because it was 
essentially a normal finding and not a structural tear of the shoulder. He indicated additional 
surgery would not benefit Petitioner's clinical symptoms/complaints. Dr. Mall also noted there was 
no evidence of Petitioner having participated in any further physical therapy following evaluation 
by Dr. Bell on October 17, 2024 (Respondent's Exhibit 3; Deposition Exhibit 4). 
 
Dr. Bell was deposed on June 16, 2025, and his deposition testimony was received into evidence 
at trial. On direct examination, Dr. Bell's testimony was consistent with his medical records and 
he reaffirmed the opinions contained therein. Specifically, Dr. Bell explained why he 
recommended a second arthroscopic surgery on Petitioner's right shoulder. He testified that the 
ultrasound of September 18, 2024, revealed a small area of the supraspinatus that had not 
completely healed or was partially tearing on the articular side. Dr. Bell stated the arthroscopy was 
26IWCC0140

Dan Koetting v. TMS International                                                   23 WC 26445 
Page 7 
also a diagnostic tool and, if it was determined that there was a small partial tear that had not 
healed, he would debride it again and put a graft over it (Petitioner's Exhibit 8; pp 15-18). 
 
Dr. Bell testified the ultrasound showed there may be some partial tearing and there was a chance 
that the tear might be more significant than what the ultrasound indicated. He stated Petitioner was 
still having pain complaints related to that tendon and that is why he recommended a "second 
look." (Petitioner's Exhibit 8; pp 20-21). 
 
On cross-examination, Dr. Bell agreed that the tear was small, but could be seen on the ultrasound. 
While the tear was 4 to 6 mm, Dr. Bell pointed out the tendon itself is, at most, 10 to 16 mm, so a 
tear of 4 to 6 mm could be 30 to 50% of the width of the tendon. Because of the preceding, Dr. 
Bell stated it could cause Petitioner to experience pain and that he gave Petitioner the benefit of 
the doubt that his shoulder was still hurting (Petitioner's Exhibit 8; pp 27-28). 
 
Dr. Bell agreed he had not seen Petitioner since November 21, 2024. Prior to proceeding with the 
second arthroscopic surgery, Dr. Bell stated he would need to see Petitioner again and that another 
ultrasound would be appropriate (Petitioner's Exhibit 8; pp 31-32). 
 
Dr. Mall was deposed on June 30, 2025, and his deposition testimony was received into evidence 
at trial. On direct examination, Dr. Mall's testimony was consistent with his medical reports and 
he reaffirmed the opinions contained therein. Specifically, Dr. Mall testified he did not agree with 
Dr. Bell's recommendation that Petitioner undergo a second arthroscopic surgery. He stated that 
the tear was not a structural tear and was not something which would require additional surgery. 
Dr. Mall testified Petitioner could return to work, but if he did not believe he could return to work 
at full duty, a Functional Capacity Evaluation should be performed (Respondent's Exhibit 3; pp 
30-32). 
 
On cross-examination, when questioned about the tear, Dr. Mall testified he would not even 
classify it as a "tear" because it was 6 x 4 mm and was "…like tendinopathy." In addition to Dr. 
Mall not agreeing with Dr. Bell's surgical recommendation, he also stated Petitioner's pain was not 
coming from the rotator cuff (Respondent's Exhibit 3; pp 41-43). 
 
At trial, Petitioner testified his right shoulder hurts all of the time. Petitioner stated he is unable to 
carry objects, including groceries, and is not able to engage in various recreational activities, 
including boating, swimming, and hunting. Petitioner has not been able to return to work and wants 
to proceed with the surgery as recommended by Dr. Bell. 
 
On cross-examination, Petitioner was questioned about his smoking and he stated he had 
previously quit, but began again while being treated by Dr. Bell. Petitioner stated he started 
smoking because of the stress he had experienced shortly after his wife died. He was also 
interrogated about being diabetic, but he stated he was no longer diabetic and was taken off all 
diabetic medication. Petitioner agreed he still owns a boat, but, because of his right shoulder 
condition, he has not been able to use it. 
 
Conclusions of Law 
 
26IWCC0140

Dan Koetting v. TMS International                                                   23 WC 26445 
Page 8 
In regard to disputed issue (F) the Arbitrator makes the following conclusion of law: 
 
The Arbitrator concludes Petitioner's current condition of ill-being in respect to his right shoulder 
is causally related to the accident of April 20, 2023. 
 
In support of this conclusion the Arbitrator notes the following: 
 
There was no dispute Petitioner sustained a work-related accident on April 20, 2023, which 
resulted in an injury to his right shoulder. 
 
Following the accident of April 20, 2023, Petitioner was treated by Dr. Robert Bell who performed 
surgery on Petitioner's right shoulder on January 12, 2024. There was no dispute regarding the 
reasonableness or necessity of that surgery and its relationship to the accident of April 20, 2023. 
 
Subsequent to the surgery of January 12, 2024, Petitioner continued to be treated by Dr. Bell and 
received extensive conservative care including physical therapy and work hardening/conditioning, 
but he has continued to complain of right shoulder pain. 
 
The ultrasound performed on September 18, 2024, revealed a small tear of the anterior 
supraspinatus.  Both Dr. Bell and Dr. Mall, Respondent's Section 12 examiner, agreed that the 
ultrasound revealed such a tear; but they disagreed as to its clinical significance. 
 
Dr. Bell opined that while the tear is "extremely small", it could be as much as 30 to 50% of the 
total width of the tendon. Because of Petitioner' ongoing complaints/symptoms, Dr. Bell 
recommended a second arthroscopic procedure be performed.   
 
Dr. Mall has opined the tear should not even be classified as a "tear," but is "…like tendinopathy." 
He does not agree with Dr. Bell's recommendation Petitioner undergo a second arthroscopic 
procedure.  However, when Dr. Mall evaluated Petitioner on August 14, 2024, and recommended 
another ultrasound be performed, he opined that if it was determined that the rotator cuff was not 
healed, a revision procedure might be necessary. 
 
Dr. Mall also noted Petitioner did not receive physical therapy subsequent to his examination with 
Dr. Bell on October 17, 2024; however, as noted herein, Petitioner received physical therapy/work 
hardening from November 5, 2024, through December 2, 2024. 
 
Petitioner’s testimony regarding his ongoing right shoulder complaints was credible and his history 
of smoking and diabetes would not have any relevance/significance in making a determination as 
to causality.   
 
Based upon the preceding, the Arbitrator finds the opinion of Dr. Bell to be more persuasive than 
that of Dr. Mall in respect to causality.   
 
In regard to disputed issue (K) the Arbitrator makes the following conclusion of law: 
 
26IWCC0140

Dan Koetting v. TMS International                                                   23 WC 26445 
Page 9 
Based upon the Arbitrator’s Conclusion of Law in disputed issue (F), the Arbitrator concludes 
Petitioner is entitled to prospective medical treatment including, but not limited to, diagnostic tests 
and arthroscopic surgery as recommended by Dr. Bell.
